about: Rows layered over the cosmos port by pricing/port-from-cosmos.ts, where a vendor's published list prices differ from, or are missing in, cosmos src/shared/model-pricing.ts: OpenAI's (Standard tier), Google's Gemini API pages (Standard paid tier, text / image / video) and Alibaba Cloud Model Studio's (Singapore, International deployment) for the Gemini CLI and Qwen Code models; and, for models the other harnesses' sessions name, Anthropic's (the Claude API table: Claude Sonnet 4's spellings and Warp's family-last Claude ids), Cognition's Devin model page (the SWE-2 and SWE-2 Flash list prices), Z.ai's (GLM-5.3, GLM-5.3-Flash and GLM-5.3-FlashX), the Kimi API platform's (Kimi K3), MiniMax's (MiniMax-M3.1-Flash and MiniMax-M3, Standard tier), OpenCode Console's (Big Pickle, which its table lists Free: $0 on every class while it does) GitHub Copilot's models-and-pricing page (MAI-Code-1.1-Flash, which Microsoft bills at that list price) and OpenRouter's (its `:free` variants, each listed at zero: $0 on every class). A Google model with implicit caching only has no write price and writes at its input rate; a Qwen model on Model Studio's explicit cache writes at 125% of input and reads at 10%. `intro` is the source's dated price: its rates through `until`, the row's own from the next day, which a cited line names. `change` is a dated rate change (cosmos d74141126e's): from `from` (a UTC day, inclusive, which a cited line names) the whole row bills as `change.pricing`, its own intro included. Rates are USD per 1M tokens in the source's shape: cacheWrite is the 30-minute cache write (billed on the cache_write_5m class), cacheWrite1h the 12-hour write (cache_write_1h). A model the pages list with no write price (every model before GPT-5.6: "No additional cache-write charge") writes at its input rate; one with no cached-input price ("-") reads at its input rate. longContext reprices the WHOLE request past overTokens prompt tokens (strict: over). `replace` reprices the source row whose pattern is `match` and refuses once that row no longer prices at `was`; `insert` adds a row ahead of the row whose pattern is `before`, or after every row when `before` is null. `fast` adds the Fast-mode row of the Standard row whose pattern is `of`, right ahead of it, matching only that model's `-fast` ids and priced at exactly `multiplier` x it (the Fast table: 2x, except gpt-5.5 2.5x and gpt-5-mini 1.8x); a model the Fast table does not list has no Fast row and its `-fast` ids price null. `promotion` marks a promotional price the page gives no end date for. `pages` records each page as read (sha256 of the body); quotes are verbatim lines of it, table padding collapsed, or, where a page carries its whole table on one script line (Devin's and Kimi's render client-side), a verbatim excerpt of that line. An Anthropic row carries the table's own two write prices (5-minute and 1-hour); a model whose page lists one write price bills both classes at it. `aliases` names ids no page prices that bill on an existing row at its rates (its pattern becomes `<of>|<match>`): no rates and no cites, only who decided it and when.

rows.why: The 12-hour cache write is 2.5x input (cosmos carries the 30-minute 1.25x in cacheWrite1h too); every other rate already matches the page.

quote: | Model | Short context input | Short context output | Short context cached input | Short context 30m write | Short context 12h write | Long context input | Long context output | Long context cached input | Long context 30m write | Long context 12h write |
Short context: ≤272K input tokens. Long context: >272K input tokens.

For GPT-5.6 and later, cache writes cost 1.25× the standard, uncached input-token rate for the default 30-minute lifetime. In the Responses API, you can choose a [12-hour minimum lifetime](#cache-lifetime) at a write rate of 2.5× ordinary input. Subsequent reads cost 0.1× the ordinary input rate on most of these models and 0.05× on [GPT-6.1 Sol](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-6.1-sol) and [GPT-6.1 Terra](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-6.1-terra), regardless of the selected lifetime.

rows.why: Missing: OpenRouter's free variants, the ids OpenRouter serves as `<author>/<slug>:free` (baidu/ernie-5.5-flash-preview:free, nvidia/nemotron-3.5-super-vl:free, google/gemma-4-31b-it:free, Hermes Agent's and Kilo Code's free models), each its own catalog entry with its own price, listed zero for prompt and completion tokens and no cache price, so every class bills $0: OpenRouter's list price for the id, as the owner decided on 2026-11-13 (hosted models at their vendor's list price). Matched only in OpenRouter's id form (an author, a slash, a slug, `:free`; an `openrouter/` or `openrouter:` prefix and a [...] tag allowed), and last in the table, so a `:free` spelling of a model a row above prices keeps that row's price, and a Claude wire id (`<author>/claude-…:free`, which the family fallback prices) is excluded: a `:free` label never lowers a listed model's price. Ids without the variant (baidu/ernie-5.5-flash-preview), OpenCode's `-free` names and the openrouter/free router stay unpriced. OpenRouter bills a fallback to a paid model at that model's price, so a session that names the paid id is priced on it.

quote: The `:free` variant allows you to access free versions of models on OpenRouter.

Append `:free` to the ID of a model that has a free entry. `:free` is a [catalog variant](https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/routing/model-variants/overview.md), so the free version appears as its own entry in the [models API](https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/overview/models.md) with its own pricing, context length, and endpoints, and only models that list one support it:
Free variants provide access to models without cost, but may have different rate limits or availability compared to paid versions.

aliases.why: The Muse app's usage rows (muse.db agent.agents.model) name Meta's internal route ids (ipnext/…), and Muse names its model Muse Spark or Muse Spark 1.3. Meta publishes no price for any ipnext/ id, and the display names are no API id. By the owner's decision of 2026-11-12 to require a Muse app entry's usage, they bill as a stand-in on the muse-spark row, the Meta Model API's published Muse Spark rate in cosmos's table, so that usage prices. The display names are matched whole.
